notes: nefesh adam is fused under rule 30's generic-head-noun clause, the ASV writing one word for the pair.

The competing reading gives body to nefesh and leaves met only the dead; it was rejected because the ASV writes a dead body for a bare met with no nefesh present, and the fused reading keeps the English order monotone with the Hebrew.
kol takes any under rule 15, being itself what the determiner renders, and the apodosis waw is unrepresented, the ASV opening the clause bare (rule 14).
